November 22

15 For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin. 16 Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need. (Hebrews 4:15-16 KJV)

Since Jesus is our High Priest in Heaven, if you are born again, and since He was a man on this earth, we now have a High Priest that understands all our temptations and feelings. Even though Jesus was God in the flesh, He was also human, and yet was without sin. He is the only human that ever existed since Adam’s creation that was born without a sin nature, and then lived a holy life, without ever committing a sin. This is the reason that He was qualified to be our sacrifice, as He was sinless. Jesus is the only one to ever fulfill all the requirements of the Old Testament Law and commandments (Matthew 5:17). He came not to do away with the law, but to fulfill it, and He did perfectly. By fulfilling all the law, and then giving us His righteousness (Romans 3:22), we have now fulfilled all the law through Jesus – Praise God, as we could not keep the law ourselves.

How many of us walk boldly into the presence of God? Most all Christians still have not purged their conscience (Hebrew 9:14) and therefore feel unworthy of coming into the very presence of God. As born again Christians, we have been given a brand new spirit, that was created holy and perfect, and since God is a Spirit (John 4:24) and looks on us in the spiritual realm, then He sees us as being holy, just like Jesus is, as we have His Spirit (Galatians 4:6). Religion continues to try and make Christians feel condemned and unholy, and tries to keep us under the law mentality. God does not look upon our actions or judge us by what we do (Hebrews 10:17), but looks upon what Jesus did for us, and we need to realize that God loves us unconditionally, no matter what we do. We need to live holy, but not so God will be pleased with us, but to keep the devil from coming into our lives with sickness and problems (John 10:10). Thank you Jesus, for doing what we could not do, and bringing us back into fellowship with the Father.

I was really fat when I graduated Grad school. Law school didn't help, I got fattened up even more. Practically all we did was eat, sleep, and study. When I exited Law School, I was 315 pounds. I was huge. My biggest reason to change happened when I noticed that my ability to sleep properly had all but vanished. I was sinking so far into the bed that I was being forced by gravity to have to sleep in the middle.

Losing weight is not an impossible task, I'm borderline autistic and I did it over time relatively easily. It first starts with a change of mindset. I used to love eating desserts when I would go out to eat. I started to ease myself into it my refusing to eat desserts at all. I would still keep my soda consumption high, but that I would change later.

I started going to the gym for 3 days out of the week, and the biggest weight loss catalyst was not the cheap apartment gym that I had access to, it was the really nice pair of headphones that I had. My favorite music and 15 minutes on the elliptical. If I could do more, I did more. I would take breaks too. You don't have to do it all at once if you have some extra time on your hands. I started working my way to longer and longer times on the elliptical machines. Finally, I was able to get to an hour without breaks. I was starting to lose weight, but it wasn't enough.

The big commitment comes when you decide to change your diet. Diet is 90% of weight loss. Exercise is 10%. I started the Atkins diet because a friend told me of his previous success. To really get the full benefits of the Atkin's diet, you have to eat a lot of meat and cheese, and prepare your toilet for a massive assault. It helps if you have a favorite burger place, and can get your burgers, to quote In-N-Out, "protein style," basically meat and cheese wrapped in lettuce. I always asked for extra lettuce wrap just because I used to eat extra lettuce separately, on some days I would hack everything up together and eat them like a salad. Eggs are also your best friend, eat tons of them for breakfast. Be wary of places like IHOP, which mix pancake batter in with their eggs, be sure to ask for whole eggs only. Bacon is okay, and amazing. Don't go overboard with it, but eating it a few times a week with breakfast is perfectly fine, just avoid bread.

When it comes to bread, there's a lot of options available to you, but they come at a higher price. Places like Ultimate Sports Nutrition and several other stores sell Atkins friendly bread, from companies like the Great Low Carb Bread Company. This will not taste like normal bread, so forget about the taste of bread for a while and try to eat these. There's plenty of varieties, including pie and pizza crusts. I used to make my own pizza sauce out of tomato sauce and spices, which is technically not diet friendly, but I would focus on topping with a lot of cheese, which is. The pizza was great for getting rid of cravings. You can even find bread sticks and butter them up and top them with garlic salt and seasonings to get a very authentic Italian feel, especially if you have some pizza sauce to dip them into. The breads made by the low carb companies are basically just fiber, which helps to clean your insides and keep them moving from all the meat and cheese. You need to keep your insides clean, because a diet of meat and cheese alone with make you unhealthy after a while, especially if you're older.

There's also plenty of special pastas that you can buy that are low carb. These are especially great when you look for a great low carb arrabiata sauce. My personal favorite was an arrabiata sauce made by that famous New York chef, I forget his name though. Marco? Mario? I used to pan fry some fresh whole mushrooms in garlic and butter and seasonings, throw a small amount of spinach in there, and then place those into a glass pan with the low carb spaghetti with plenty of sauce and top with cheddar, mozzarella, and Parmesan.

I did all this while maintaining a strict exercise regimen. I got really good at long distance running, and then switched to doing HIIT workouts. Check out more about HIIT workouts here: https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=hiit+training. The HIIT workouts I did later towards the end of my desired weight loss goals.
